subject: Recap: HealthSync - Private deployment constraints and success criteria
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthsync.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: HealthSync - Private deployment constraints and success criteria

Laura — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment before the technical workshop: 

High-level pain points we heard
- Regulatory constraint: PHI must remain in an isolated on-prem/air-gapped segment (no internet egress for inference).
- Key management: customer-managed keys (HSM/Thales) required for encryption at rest and for model key wrapping.
- Auditability: 3yr retention for audit logs, per-record traceability for access and inference events.
- Network: strict outbound policy (only to approved IP ranges), existing perimeter devices (F5) and internal MinIO S3-compatible store.

Current stack you described
- OpenShift / on-prem Kubernetes (control plane in DMZ), GPU hosts (NVIDIA A100), MinIO object store, Okta for SSO, F5 LB shaping north-south traffic.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for HealthSync)
- P0: No PHI leaves the air-gapped environment during inference; customer retains full custody of keys.
- P1: Inference throughput ~200 req/min steady-state, p95 latency under 300ms for 1–2k token payloads.
- Security: Integration with your Thales HSM for active key operations; audit logs exported to your SIEM.

Technical gaps we need to validate in the workshop
- Which ports and IP ranges can be opened for the Redwood control path (if any) and whether a proxy or outbound-only gateway is permitted.
- Exact HSM model and integration method (KMIP vs. PKCS#11).
- Acceptable installer pattern: full air-gap bundle (tar + install scripts) vs. pull from internal registry.

Proposed next steps (please confirm)
- Technical workshop with your security and infra teams: Wed Apr 14, 10:00 AM PT (I’ve proposed on our side).
- You to share a network topology (MinIO location, LB placement, VLAN segmentation) before the call — upload to the Drive link below.
- We’ll provide a short security questionnaire and a private-deployment checklist (attached).

Attachments: redwood-private-checklist.pdf (installer options, required ports, certs/HSM notes)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Hsh-example-drive-link

Thanks — I’ll coordinate calendar invites once you confirm the time.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
redwood.ai

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthsync.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@healthsync.com>, it-support@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HealthSync - Private deployment constraints and success criteria

Mina — thanks for the clear recap. Confirmations and clarifications below: 

Confirmations
- Air-gapped requirement is firm for PHI processing: inference must be able to run without any public internet egress. Any outbound control traffic must be limited to pre-authorized Redwood control IPs and go through our outbound proxy.
- We will require HSM integration (Thales nShield, model T520) and prefer KMIP where supported.
- Audit logs need to be forwarded to our Splunk cluster (on-prem) with a retention policy of 3 years.

Clarifications / asks
- Can Redwood support an installer flow that runs entirely from an internal artifact registry? (we cannot allow package pulls from the internet during install).
- For latency: our internal target is p95 < 300ms as you noted — we’ll need a test harness during PoC to validate under 200 req/min baseline and burst to 600 req/min.

I’ve CC’d Dr. Amir Qureshi (Head of Compliance) and our infra alias (it-support) — Amir, can you share any additional non-functional requirements we missed?

Attached: healthsync-network-diagram.pdf (simplified VLAN/LB placement)

Laura Chen
Director, Platform Engineering | HealthSync Inc.
laura.chen@healthsync.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Dr. Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@healthsync.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthsync.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: it-support@healthsync.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HealthSync - Private deployment constraints and success criteria

Thanks Laura and Mina. A couple of compliance items we need Redwood to address prior to procurement review: 

1) Key custody and HSM details — we need documentation that describes how key material is generated, stored, wrapped, and whether Redwood retains any bootstrap keys. If Redwood uses a PKI bootstrap, we cannot accept in cleartext over the network.

2) Audit log format — sample of log schema for inference events (timestamp, user/actor, model id/version, input hash, output hash, request metadata). We need assurances logs are tamper-evident and can be exported to our SIEM.

3) Certifications / attestations — do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports or a summary that we can review? If not, provide the security questionnaire you mentioned.

4) Proof of air-gap support — specifically, a description of an install path and runtime confirmation that inference traffic can be restricted to the isolated VLAN with no egress.

Please route the above to your security team; we’ll add procurement once these are answered.

Dr. Amir Qureshi
Head of Compliance | HealthSync Inc.
amir.qureshi@healthsync.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@healthsync.com>, Dr. Amir Qureshi <amir.qureshi@healthsync.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: HealthSync - Private deployment constraints and success criteria

Laura / Amir — appreciate the details. Quick responses and next actions from Redwood: 

- Installer / air-gap: We support an air-gapped install bundle that can be pushed to an internal registry. We will not require outbound package pulls. (See attached workshop agenda for options.)
- HSM: Our integration paths include KMIP (preferred), PKCS#11, and an operator pattern for on-prem Thales. Rishi (cc’d) will surface a short integration note prior to the workshop. Please confirm the exact Thales firmware/driver version if possible.
- Audit logs: we can emit structured JSON logs for inference events and provide an HMAC-based append-only log export to your SIEM. We’ll bring a sample log schema to the workshop.
- Certifications: Rishi will attach our SOC 2 summary and ISO attestation excerpt to the HubSpot deal; we’ll also send the security questionnaire ahead of the call.

Proposed workshop
- Date: Wed Apr 14
- Time: 10:00 AM PT (60 min)
- Attendees: Mina (Solutions), Rishi (Security), Dev (Infra ops), Laura (Platform), Amir (Compliance), HealthSync infra team

Action items for HealthSync before the call
- Share final network topology + Thales model/firmware (upload to Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Hsh-example-drive-link
- Confirm the outbound proxy/policy details and any IP allowlist constraints.

We’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read (security questionnaire + checklist). Looking forward to the workshop.

Best,
Mina
